findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117: `align-items` omits `-moz-box-align`, so layouts using the `display: -moz-box` fallback will not be vertically centered in affected Firefox versions

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:117: `align-items` omits `-moz-box-align`, so layouts using the `display: -moz-box` fallback will not be vertically centered in affected Firefox versions

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the `@mixin align-items` at line 117 includes `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but does NOT include `-moz-box-align`. Since the `@mixin flexbox()` includes `display: -moz-box` as a fallback for older Firefox versions, the alignment mixin should correspondingly include `-moz-box-align` for consistency. Without it, elements using the `-moz-box` display fallback won't have proper vertical alignment in those Firefox versions. This is a real cross-browser compatibility bug.
